articles.title: Unshaped Aether
articles.description: In Aetherforge’s oldest creation traditions, the Unshaped Aether was an elemental storm that preceded land and sky.

articles.title: First Spark
articles.description: Creation tradition describes the First Spark as a point of impossible heat that became the Eternal Forge.

articles.title: Eternal Forge
articles.description: In myth, the Eternal Forge responds to struggle, pressure, conflict and determination.

articles.title: Kharadon
articles.description: Kharadon is revered as King of Dragons and Keeper of the Eternal Forge. His ancient sovereignty stands apart from the six divisional dragons and the ordinary Ladder hierarchy.

articles.title: Aurelith
articles.description: Aurelith is associated in tradition with Titanium and the ideal of precision.

articles.title: Drakhar
articles.description: Drakhar is associated in tradition with Cinder and the ideal of persistence.

articles.title: Pyrakon
articles.description: Pyrakon is associated in tradition with Ember and the ideal of ambition.

articles.title: Seraphyne
articles.description: Seraphyne is associated in tradition with Damascus and mastery through creation.

articles.title: Varkyros
articles.description: Varkyros is associated in tradition with Obsidian and the ideal of dominion.

articles.title: Veyrath
articles.description: Veyrath is associated in tradition with Ash and recovery after ruin.

articles.title: Seven Lessons of Ascension
articles.description: The traditional lessons are Ignition — Begin; Ash — Rise; Cinder — Endure; Ember — Hunger; Damascus — Master; Titanium — Perfect; and Obsidian — Reign. Ascend belongs to Kharadon beyond these stages.

articles.title: The Six Kingdoms
articles.description: Aetherforge’s six kingdoms are Ash, Cinder, Ember, Damascus, Titanium and Obsidian. Tradition associates them respectively with Veyrath, Drakhar, Pyrakon, Seraphyne, Aurelith and Varkyros. Ignition is a gateway outside the six.

articles.title: Ash
articles.description: Ash is associated in tradition with recovery after ruin and the dragon Veyrath. Its landscape includes pale forests, ruined towers, waterfalls and new construction among old ruins.

articles.title: Cinder
articles.description: Cinder is associated in tradition with Drakhar and persistence. A hammer on a coal-red shield appears as its heraldry.

articles.title: Ember
articles.description: Ember is one of the six kingdoms, associated in tradition with Pyrakon and ambition.

articles.title: Damascus
articles.description: Damascus is one of the six kingdoms, associated in tradition with Seraphyne and mastery through creation.

articles.title: Titanium
articles.description: Titanium is one of the six kingdoms, associated in tradition with Aurelith and precision.

articles.title: Obsidian
articles.description: Obsidian is one of the six kingdoms, associated in tradition with Varkyros and dominion.

articles.title: Ascension Bridges
articles.description: Ascension Bridges are ancient, permanent magical passages at fixed locations. They compress distance; travelers physically walk across them and emerge at designated arrival platforms. They are normally convenient and safe to traverse.

articles.title: Ash arrival platform
articles.description: The Ash arrival platform is a broad black stone landing overlooking the kingdom’s ruins.

articles.title: Crown Grounds
articles.description: The Crown Grounds are the ceremonial arena within Vaelorian Citadel, with descending terraces, plazas, galleries and stone courts surrounding a central arena and dais.

articles.title: Kharadon’s Summit
articles.description: In foundational tradition, Kharadon’s Summit is the ultimate destination of Ascension.

articles.title: Sparkhaven
articles.description: Sparkhaven is approached by a bridge that arrives outside the city. Its approach features cobblestone, basalt, obsidian and black volcanic walls; the gate bears the motto “Every Legend Begins With a Spark.” Its atmosphere is warm and dry, with the scent of forge and bread.

articles.title: Vaelorian Citadel
articles.description: Vaelorian Citadel is described in tradition as a neutral capital and ceremonial center outside divisional sovereignty.

articles.title: Ignition
articles.description: Ignition is a gateway outside the six kingdoms, with no permanent divisional rank or dragon of its own.

articles.title: Ladder of Legends
articles.description: Foundational tradition describes the Ladder of Legends as a series of tests proposed by Kharadon in place of endless rivalry and war.

articles.title: Crucibles
articles.description: Crucibles are competitions that predate the founding of FYI.

articles.title: Daggers
articles.description: Competitive daggers physically record achievements, ownership and competitive history in modern Aetherforge.

articles.title: Administrative Council
articles.description: The Administrative Council is the principal mortal governing body. It oversees competition, community, administration, records and technical systems alongside ancient dragon authority. Other members handle decisions directly affecting a member’s competitive interests.

articles.title: Magic
articles.description: Extraordinary magic exists within Aetherforge’s medieval high-fantasy setting. The Ascension Bridges are an established example of magical travel; specific equipment mechanisms are not established.

articles.title: Obsidian (material)
articles.description: Obsidian appears on Sparkhaven’s volcanic approach and as a material used for clubheads. Its precise metallurgy is not established.

articles.title: Golden Dragons
articles.description: Golden dragons are a currency denomination in Aetherforge. The available canon does not establish a general exchange rate or price scale.
